title: Tensile deformation behavior and mechanical properties of a bulk cast Al0.9CoFeNi2 eutectic high-entropy alloy

nodes.label: Structural high-entropy alloys need strength and tensile ductility at once, and a castable bulk route rather than a laboratory arc-melted button
How the two eutectic phases divide the deformation, and how their dislocation substructures evolve with strain, has not been followed in a Cr-free eutectic HEA
A lamellar eutectic of a soft ordered FCC and a hard B2 should deform in stages, the soft phase first, and so combine high strength with useful ductility
Al0.9CoFeNi2, the Cr-free counterpart of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA
Interrupt the tensile test at 0.6%, 1.5% and at fracture and take TEM of both lamellae at each stage

attrs.note: the staged substructure record is the paper's contribution

nodes.label: Bulk casting by medium-frequency induction melting under argon
Uniaxial tension at 1e-3 /s at room temperature, stopped at 0.6% and 1.5% strain and finally taken to fracture
The as-cast alloy is a dual-phase ordered FCC (L12) plus ordered BCC (B2) structure
A full eutectic cell morphology: a flat coarse band through the cell centre surrounded by regular two-phase lamellae 1-2 um wide
About 60 vol.% FCC (L12) and 40 vol.% B2
The FCC lamellae are enriched in Fe and Co, the B2 lamellae in Al and Ni
At 0.6% strain dislocations appear only in the FCC lamellae and bank up at the FCC/B2 boundaries; the B2 stays free of them
At 1.5% the FCC dislocation density is much higher and carries slip bands, boundary pile-ups, intersections and networks; the B2 is still free
After fracture the FCC holds dense Taylor lattices and dislocation walls, and straight dislocations have finally appeared in the B2 as well
Yield strength 559 MPa, ultimate tensile strength 1005 MPa and 6.2% tensile elongation at room temperature
Work hardening runs in three stages and adds 446 MPa between yield and ultimate strength, which delays necking
Fracture is mixed: ductile tearing along the FCC lamellae with flat brittle-like facets on the B2 lamellae and voids on the phase boundaries
The soft FCC yields first; dislocations bank up against the B2 lamellae, and the back stress of those pile-ups sets the high yield strength
Accumulating bands, networks and walls in the FCC hold the hardening rate up through stage II; when the boundary stress reaches the B2 yield strength the B2 gives way and stage III begins
A bulk-cast Cr-free eutectic HEA reaches 1005 MPa with 6.2% elongation because its two lamellar phases yield in sequence and the soft phase hardens steadily
Removing Cr leaves the dual-phase L12 + B2 structure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 unchanged
The staged substructures come from one specimen per strain and from single fields, and the two phases are imaged at different magnifications
Marker sticks assign the pattern to L12 and B2, but only the three strong reflections near 44, 51 and 91 deg rise clearly above background

Dark dislocation tangles line the lamella boundaries, a dark band runs along one lamella, and the interiors carry cell walls and intersecting dislocation lines

nodes.label: The lamella interiors are filled with curved, tangled cell walls rather than the straight coplanar arrays that define planar slip

attrs.image_note: cell-like walls are the signature of wavy slip and easy cross slip, which cuts against the paper's low stacking-fault-energy, difficult-cross-slip reading of the same panels

nodes.label: The FCC lamella after fracture holds dense crossing dislocation arrays forming a regular grid, with an arrow on a pile-up at the left boundary
The B2 lamella after fracture carries two crossing families of long straight dislocations at high density

attrs.image_note: the text describes a single straight, parallel set; the panel shows two crossing families

nodes.label: The two post-fracture panels are taken at 0.5 um and 0.2 um scale bars, so the claim that the FCC dislocation density exceeds the B2 one cannot be read from this pair
SEM-EDS gives the FCC lamellae rich in Fe and Co and the B2 lamellae rich in Al and Ni
The AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA has the same FCC (L12) plus B2 dual-phase lamellar structure
Planar dislocation configurations such as slip bands and coplanar arrays indicate a low stacking-fault energy and difficult cross slip
The ordered FCC (L12) phase is the soft, ductile constituent and the B2 phase the hard, brittle one
Dislocations banked against a boundary generate a back stress that raises the stress needed for further slip

notes: The spine is the staged substructure record: DES/method (interrupted tensile tests plus TEM) is on the spine and realizes the 1.5% substructure claim, and the three STR/defect/extended nodes follow one another by causes along the strain axis. Lost: Table 1 (per-phase EDS), the gauge geometry, and the stress-partition arithmetic behind the 446 MPa hardening figure. Image findings: the XRD superlattice markers for L12 and most B2 markers sit on a flat baseline, so the ordering claim rests on the SAED, not on F1a (g1); the EBSD map is stepped at 0.5 um against 1-2 um lamellae, so the 60/40 split is coarsely sampled (g3); the 0.2% offset construction that gives the quoted 559 MPa is not drawn (g5); the lamella interiors at 1.5% show curved, tangled cell walls, the signature of wavy slip, which cuts against the paper's planar-slip / low-SFE reading (g11); the two post-fracture panels are at different magnifications, so the claimed higher dislocation density in the FCC phase cannot be read from them (g14); the B2 panel shows two crossing dislocation families rather than one parallel set (g13); the markings on F2d are not explained in the caption (g7). Panel section: the F2b crop is labelled 'letter a (OCR DISAGREES with detector b)' and the F5b crop 'letter q'; both are really (b).

changes: g14: removed attrs.aspect = 'outlier'. aspect=outlier is an mm_op attribute of cross_check_consistency (r04 ruling #7) and belongs on the edge, and in any case this node does not set a deviating point aside - it reports that a comparison cannot be made because the two panels are at different magnifications.

panel_checks.note: the hardening-rate panel starts at about 85 GPa, falls to about 14 GPa at the stage I/II dashed line near true strain 0.009, declines to about 5 GPa by 0.057 and drops to about -10 GPa; the inset true-stress curve ends near 1080 MPa at 0.06. Every number in the node is on the panel. Note the packet labels this crop 'letter a (OCR DISAGREES with detector b)': the crop is (b), and the graph is right to use F2b.

the lamella interior is filled with curved, closed cell walls, not straight coplanar arrays, so the wavy-slip reading that cuts against the paper's low-SFE argument is what the panel shows. The in-panel 'Dislocations pileup' label that g10 reports is on this crop.

F5b is the post-fracture B2 panel (0.2 um bar). It shows a dominant family of long straight parallel dislocations with a second, darker set inclined across it, so image_support = partial and the node's disagreement with the text's 'single parallel set' is fair. The packet labels this crop 'letter q'; it is (b).

review.audit_summary: 3 audits (f22 method limitation, g11 the wavy-slip signature contradicting the paper's planar-slip reading, g14 the magnification mismatch). g11 is the valuable one and is stated correctly as 'the panel shows X, which cuts against the paper's reading', not as an error. g14 correctly distinguishes 'the figure does not resolve it' from 'the figure contradicts the text'.
